title: Pesticides and Cancer Risk
summary: Reviews pesticide and cancer evidence: organic diets cut pesticide levels, but produce benefits outweigh residue risks.

assertions.quote: you can turn on and off urinary concentrations of pesticide metabolites like a light switch
the benefits of consuming conventionally grown produce are likely to outweigh any possible risks from pesticide exposure
has been estimated to only cut a few minutes off a person's life, on average
this class of chlorinated pesticides are fat soluble, so they're found most frequently in foods of animal origin

verdicts.note: Persistent organochlorines, dioxins and PCBs build up in animal fat, and most dietary exposure comes from meat, dairy and fish.

assertions.quote: most of the evidence that shows DNA damage from pesticides is from occupational exposure among farmers and workers in the fields

verdicts.note: Studies of applicators and farm workers link high exposure to some pesticides with cancers such as non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
The paper notes occupational pesticide exposure has been linked to NHL, soft tissue sarcoma and breast cancer, but 'albeit not conclusively'.

For one pesticide, glyphosate, occupational studies across regions and formulations reported similar increases in non-Hodgkin lymphoma, backed by animal and genotoxicity data; IARC still rates the human evidence 'limited'.
